newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-BECKER SUCCUMBS TO INJURY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER SUCCUMBS TO INJURY AGAIN.

text.p: Boris Becker, playing his first tournament since rupturing a wrist tendon, succumbed to injury again in the third round of the Japan Open on Thursday.
The German second seed pulled his right thigh muscle while leading 16th-seeded Frenchman Lionel Roux 6-4 2-0. Roux went on to win 4-6 6-3 6-1.
"It was very frustrating. I mean I had him on the ropes 6-4 2-0 and I was cruising, then it happened... on one right forehand I felt it pull and I only won two games after that," Becker said.
But Becker said the tendon injury had not been a problem during his one doubles and two singles matches in the tournament.
"The main concern was always my wrist, which is fine right now," Becker said.
"I guess the problem with my leg is from not playing in a while and I wasn't used to a couple of matches in a row like that. But I'm still up for Monte Carlo, Hamburg and then Rome."
The 29-year-old former Wimbledon champion said age had not been a factor in his injury.
"Twenty-one year olds are injured as well. I don't think that's the problem. I've had a lot of wear and tear but I also take very good care of myself," he said.
"The leg should be fine in a couple of days... the main concern is to get your body in the best possible shape and you only get better by playing competitions."
Roux said a changeable wind on the Ariake centre court had played a part in his victory.
"I think we both didn't play very good tennis today. I just tried to put the ball in the court and try to hit the ball in the middle of the court," Roux said.
"I didn't give a lot of points to Boris and that's why maybe I won this match."
Top seed and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek beat 15th seed Magnus Norman of Sweden 7-5 6-0 after leading 3-1 in the first set.
"I could have broken him but I let him back into the set and then he started to play pretty good and it was tough," Krajicek said.
In the women's quarter-finals, fourth seed Ai Sugiyama beat American Corina Morariu 7-6 6-2 after a gruelling first set with several delightful rallies.
Sugiyama faces number one seed Kimberly Po while third seeded American Amy Frazier is up against Australian wild card Annabel Ellwood in Friday's semifinals.
